samples.summary: Peer-controlled presence position (now including `lineAffinity`) is forwarded into rendering with no runtime validation
samples.evidence: Threat model: any collaborator attached to the Yorkie document controls their own presence payload verbatim. `buildPeerCursors` at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:226 passes `p.presence.activeCursorPos!` straight through as `PeerCursor.position`, and this change makes editor.ts:1564 read `peer.position.lineAffinity` (previously a hardcoded `'backward'`) and feed it into `resolvePositionPixel`, where it becomes `affinity` (peer-cursor.ts:111). The declared union `'forward' | 'backward'` (packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:29) is compile-time only — a peer can publish any JSON value (e.g. an object, or a huge string). I traced the consumption: the value is only ever compared with `=== 'forward'` (peer-cursor.ts:206, and via `findPageForPosition`), so a hostile value degenerates to the backward reading and I could NOT construct an exploit — no injection sink, no unbounded loop, no prototype-pollution vector (object spread of `{...pos}` in cursor.ts defines own properties rather than setting `__proto__`). Reported as hardening only: this repo already treats presence as forgeable elsewhere (`sanitizeDisplayName` / `sanitizeWrittenAt` in packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:34-38, explicitly citing forged peer presence), so a peer-supplied enum crossing into the docs render path without an equivalent whitelist is an inconsistency in the trust boundary, and it widens what remote data influences local rendering.
searchedFor: read peer-cursor.ts resolvePositionPixel (lines 80-220) to trace every use of the affinity value

samples.summary: `getPresenceCursorPos()` casts raw presence JSON to `DocPosition` with no validation, and the undo/redo consumers clamp only the upper bound of `offset`
samples.evidence: `getPresenceCursorPos()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2922 and :2930) does `(presence as Record<string, unknown>)?.activeCursorPos as DocPosition | undefined` — an unchecked cast of a value that comes back from the CRDT layer. The change widens the declared return type to the full `DocPosition`, so the spread consumers added in this diff (editor.ts ~2032 and ~2064: `cursor.moveTo({ ...restoredPos, offset: Math.min(restoredPos.offset, maxOffset) })`) now copy every own property of that untrusted-shaped object onto the caret, and the offset is clamped only from above (`Math.min`), never with `Math.max(0, …)` or a `Number.isFinite` check, so a negative/NaN/non-numeric offset would propagate into layout math. I could not complete an attacker chain: this path reads the *local* client's own presence (`getMyPresence()` / `getPresenceForTest(ownActorId)`), which a remote peer cannot write in Yorkie, so I found no way for a third party to inject the value — hence low confidence and minor severity. Worth a `Math.max(0, …)` plus a shape check for defence in depth given the value is deserialized rather than constructed locally.
searchedFor: read clampPosToModel at yorkie-doc-store.ts:957-977 to see where clamping does happen
